_what: How often chance alone would produce the alignment each study measured, as the paper's own abstract gives it. Read by the odds chart on the probability page.
_src: abstract: the number is quoted from the paper's abstract (see quote); derived: converted by us from the quoted value (99.6% confidence is a 0.4% chance). A study whose abstract gives no number has p null and is drawn as 'consistent with chance' with no mark. Checked against the PDFs in papers/ on 2026-10-30.

studies.label: Batygin & Brown 2016
studies.detail: the six founding objects, no bias correction
studies.quote: such a clustering has only a probability of 0.007% to be due to chance

studies.label: Brown & Batygin 2019
studies.detail: after modelling where the surveys looked
studies.quote: the probability that these distant Kuiper belt objects would be clustered as strongly as observed in both longitude of perihelion and in orbital pole position is only 0.2%

studies.label: Brown & Batygin 2021
studies.quote: the clustering remains significant at the 99.6% confidence level

studies.label: Napier et al. 2021
studies.detail: 14 objects from three surveys that recorded where they looked
studies.quote: consistent with a uniform population at a level between 17% and 94%

studies.label: Shankman et al. 2017
studies.detail: eight objects from one such survey
studies.quote: the orbital distribution of the OSSOS sample is consistent with being detected from a uniform underlying angular distribution
